steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: Boolean logic is a form of algebra where all values are either TRUE (1) or FALSE (0). It is named after mathematician George Boole and forms the basis of how computers make decisions. | NOT gate: Takes a single input and produces the opposite (inverted) output. If input is 1, output is 0. If input is 0, output is 1. Also called an inverter. | AND gate: Takes two inputs and outputs 1 (TRUE) only if BOTH inputs are 1. If either or both inputs are 0, the output is 0. | OR gate: Takes two inputs and outputs 1 (TRUE) if EITHER or BOTH inputs are 1. The output is 0 only when both inputs are 0.
